notes: WHAT THIS PASS WAS GIVEN AND WHAT IT FOUND. Three of his four rulings had already landed: iso back in STYLES, the hand-off hub priced on `central`, and - as a WIP commit - A SIZE FLOOR ON THAT PRICE, DHO_CEN_LO 77 -> DHO_CEN_HI 82, his words "The tighter one, full at 6'10", nothing under 6'5"." This pass re-pointed the eleven tests the moved behaviour had left stale, re-measured the frozen reference for the SHIPPED formula, and checked the one belief the dispatch asked to be checked. Everything below is a reading taken on this tree.

THE SIZE FLOOR IS THE SECOND HALF OF A TWO-PART TEST AND THAT IS WHY IT WORKS. Centrality alone cannot tell "the offence runs through this man" from "this man is a point guard": a guard IS his own five's best creator by definition, so `central` read a flat 1.00 on Haliburton exactly as on Jokic, and the men the nomination exists to keep out were handed full marks. recal_213's pinned "no guard becomes a hub" went from 0 of the fives reading the hand-off to 17. WITH THE FLOOR: 0 of 145, and the shortest hub on ANY reading five is 6'8" - Steve Smith '94, Grant Hill '96, Pippen '99/'02/'03, McGrady '05/'07/'08 - a two-inch margin under recal_213's own line rather than a boundary case. The share of the board falls 15.1% -> 11.6%. HEIGHT AND PLAYMAKING choose the hub (`hubScore`, untouched, 48 short nominations exactly as recal_226 left them); CENTRALITY TIMES SIZE says what he is worth there.

AND THAT PINNED RULE IS NOW AN ASSERTION INSTEAD OF A COMMENT. tests/tactics.test.ts carried recal_213's sentence as prose with a count in a comment; it now reads the whole wheel - 1,255 fives through startingFive and bestStyle - and asserts 48 short NOMINATIONS (the seat, unchanged), 145 reading fives, ZERO of them with a hub under 6'6", and a minimum hub height of 80 inches. That is the strongest form this rule has ever been held in and it is the form recal_213 originally wanted; the previous pass could only state it as a ranking rule on `hubScore`.

Three findings, all re-measured on this tree, so the next round starts from the reading instead of re-deriving it.

(1) A SPACING DRAG ON THE PIN-DOWN WOULD PUNISH THE WRONG TEAMS. By the engine's own cornerFit the Clippers '20 floor is BETTER spaced than the Pacers '96 - worst 41 / mean 59 against worst 34 / mean 51 on the z, worst 27 / mean 55 against worst 16 / mean 42 on the raw - and the Pacers are Reggie Miller's team, the pin-down archetype, which reads 87.39. So 'they aren't a knockdown shooting team' is not something a shooting term can be made to say about this five without taking the read off the five the set is named for.

(2) HIS OWN LINEUP CHANGE DOES MOVE THEM, AND NOT TO THE PICK-AND-ROLL. Swapping Lou Williams '20 in for Montrezl Harrell '20, exactly as he describes, takes the pin-down 82.17 -> 73.13 and from 1st to 4th. But the five then reads MOTION 85.03, with fiveout 80.03 and pickpop 73.34 ahead of the pin-down too; pnr reaches only 67.60 and balanced is 50.00 by construction. So his intuition that the pin-down is wrong for them IS reproduced, and his intuition about the destination is not.

(3) THE REAL CONTENT OF THAT RULING IS ARCHITECTURAL, AND IT IS A RULING HE HAS NOT MADE. `startingFive` picks one five and `bestStyle` then grades the twelve tactics on it, so the engine can never see that a team is a pick-and-roll team WITH A DIFFERENT LINEUP - his own parenthesis, 'a tactic/team fit can change the starting 5'. Making the tactic and the five chosen JOINTLY is a change to src/engine/bestfive.ts, not to src/engine/tactics.ts, and it would move every team's five and therefore every dial and the whole campaign ladder. It needs his word before anybody writes it.
